What bnec() did to your request before fitting

Source: R/bnec_record.R
bnec_record.Rd

Reports the candidate set as requested, the candidate set attempted, the equations excluded and why, and any substitution made in the response.

bnec_record(x)

Arguments

x

An object of class bayesnecfit or bayesmanecfit returned by bnec.

Value

A list with elements requested and attempted, both character vectors of equation names; excluded, a data.frame of the equations bnec declined to attempt with the reason for each; and substitutions, a data.frame of the changes made to the response, or NULL where none were made. requested is partitioned exactly by attempted and excluded$model.

attempted is the set bnec tried to fit, not the set that sampled: an equation that was attempted and failed appears here, and for bnec and amend also in failed_models. The name was chosen over fitted for that reason. update does not record failures, so an equation whose refit failed stays in attempted and is not reported by failed_models.

The record is kept through update and amend. NULL for an object fitted by a version that did not record it.

Details

bnec decides which of the requested equations it will not attempt, and check_data() substitutes values that a family cannot represent — a zero under Gamma or Beta, a one under Beta. Both were reported by message and then discarded, so neither could be recovered from the returned object: only from console output, which a knitted document or a call wrapped in suppressMessages does not keep. The set as requested, the set attempted, the reason for the difference, and what was altered in the data are exactly what a methods section has to state.

Two of the three substitutions were silent even on the console, so a user comparing bayesnec against another engine had no way to see that the data had been changed at all.

See also

bnec, models, check_data

Examples

# \donttest{
library(bayesnec)
data(manec_example)
bnec_record(manec_example)
#> NULL
# }
